summary: The proof establishes the stated bound without gaps. The primary source, Averkov and Weismantel, Theorem 1.1, equation (3), gives h(R^r x Z^s) = (r+1)2^s for the finite M-convex family formulation defined in its introduction, so coordinate permutation and r=1, s=n justify the Helly application to the compact convex hulls. The strict complement-weight inequalities establish every required subfamily intersection, including the case with fewer than h members, and the open-complement argument proves the atomic weighted centerpoint bound with closed-halfspace boundaries included. The explicit affine lift preserves convex-hull membership and the integer base, ensuring that the chosen point belongs to the actual body and its actual integer fiber. Reflection gives at least half the selected fiber volume, including b=0, and the atomic weights and ambient mixed-integer measure use exactly the same unnormalized mass W. Zero total mass, coincident centers, degenerate pullbacks, and boundary mass are all handled correctly.
